newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia textile firms need competitiveness boost.
newsitem.headline: Australia textile firms need competitiveness boost.

text.p: Rising domestic and export competition would force Australian textiles industries to lift their game or miss opportunities in the quality end of the market, a government think tank said on Wednesday.

Survival for many firms would depend on their ability to supply quality products to niche markets but Asia-Pacific manufacturers, jockeying for larger market shares, were offering more competition in export markets and in Australia itself.

"As a consequence of both developments, Australian firms will have to read their markets with greater skill, both to identify emerging opportunities and to ensure they have the competitive advantages to capture them," the Productivity Commission report said.
A growing number of Australian textiles, clothing and footwear (TCF) firms were already pursuing the quality end of the market.

The commission said medium-term growth opportunities for local firms appeared mixed, although they should benefit from an expected reduction in trade barriers in Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation Group (APEC) economies.
"Improved market access is likely to engender new export initiatives by some Australian TCF firms," it said.
"However, improved market access, in itself, does not guarantee commercial success in foreign markets."
The Australian government has asked the Industry Commission to compile a report on arrangements to help the TCF industries beyond the year 2000.
That report, which is giving particular attention to barriers facing Australian exports, is due out in mid-June.
